- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often overshoots early in forecast horizon; cap peak forecasts at 2–3% below recent high.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects; apply a 1–2% downward bias to subsequent 3–5 day forecasts.  
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative, model often fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast by 2–4% in the first 2–3 days of the new sentiment phase.  
- Model tends to overpredict mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if sentiment is neutral or negative, apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to the final 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating 0.67/0.33), model overfits to recent highs; use 3-day moving average of true values as a smoothing anchor.
